title: Man. Post. Cap. IX: PLAC — three replies same sound; conjunction as sinner ≠ as origin alone
pass_a_gloss: Placeus treats the learned man's three answers as one voice and refutes them together. First split the bond with the sinner: joined to him insofar as he is a sinner—by consent, propagation, or imitation—you cannot be free of that same sin. Joined to him only insofar as he is the man from whom you draw origin is a different bond and must not be confused with the first.
pass_b_english: PLAC. Those three replies of the learned man seem to me to sound the same; I will therefore refute them all together. First the conjunction with the sinner must be distinguished: for one is conjunction with the sinner insofar as he is a sinner, another with the sinner insofar as he is the man from whom we draw our origin. He cannot be free from sin who is joined with the sinner insofar as he is a sinner: for he is a partaker of the same sin, whether by consent, or by propagation, or by imitation, and so on.
source_text: PLAC. Idem sonare mihi videntur tres istae Viri docti responsiones; simul igitur omnes refellam. Principio distinguenda est coniunctio cum peccatore: alia enim est coniunctio cum peccatore quatenus est peccator, alia cum peccatore quatenus est homo a quo ducimus originem. Vacare peccato non potest qui cum peccatore coniunctus est quatenus est peccator: particeps enim est eiusdem peccati, vel consensione, vel propagatione, vel imitatione &c.

choices.choice: Bond as sinner vs bond as mere origin
